title: DET Listening: Listen and Type & Interactive Listening
summary: How the DET tests listening — precise dictation and a two-way interactive conversation — and how to score both.

nodes.label: Listen and Type
nodes.note: Type the sentence you hear, exactly

nodes.label: Replays limited
nodes.note: You can hear it only a couple of times

chunks.heading: Listen and Type — dictation, exactly
chunks.body: You **hear a spoken sentence and type it exactly**. You can replay it only a **limited number of times**, so listen for the **whole sentence** and reconstruct it — every correctly-spelled word in the right place scores.
chunks.realExample: Hear 'The lecture will begin at half past nine' → type it word-for-word. A slip like 'the lectures will begin' loses marks, so lock in the exact words and spelling.
chunks.memoryHook: Catch the whole sentence, then type it exactly. Limited replays — focus the first listen.

chunks.heading: Chunk it and hold it
chunks.body: For longer sentences, **break the audio into 3–4 word chunks** and hold them in memory, then write them out. Getting the **structure and key content words** right matters most; don't freeze over one word you missed.
chunks.realExample: Missed one word in the middle? Type the rest correctly and make your best guess for the gap — a near-complete, correctly-spelled sentence still scores well.
chunks.memoryHook: Hear in chunks, rebuild the sentence. A near-complete answer beats a frozen one.

chunks.heading: Interactive Listening — a two-way conversation
chunks.body: **Interactive Listening** puts you in a **realistic conversation**: you listen, **choose appropriate responses** as it unfolds, and then **summarise** what was discussed. It rewards following the thread and catching the speaker's intent, not just isolated words.
chunks.realExample: If the speaker proposes a meeting time and asks if it works, the right response addresses that specific point — picking a reply that ignores the question is the trap.
chunks.memoryHook: Follow the thread and answer the actual point. Then summarise the gist.

chunks.heading: Spelling and attention win listening
chunks.body: Across the listening tasks, **accurate spelling** and **sustained attention** decide your score. There's no penalty for a natural accent in your own speaking — but in Listen and Type, precise transcription is everything.
chunks.realExample: Practise by transcribing short English clips and checking every word — the habit of exact transcription is exactly what Listen and Type rewards.
chunks.memoryHook: Attention + exact spelling. Listen and Type is a transcription test, so transcribe precisely.

recall.q: What do you do in the 'Listen and Type' task?
recall.a: Type a spoken sentence exactly as you hear it, with only a limited number of replays.

recall.q: What's a good technique for longer sentences in Listen and Type?
recall.a: Break the audio into 3–4 word chunks, hold them in memory, and reconstruct the full sentence.

recall.q: What happens in the 'Interactive Listening' task?
recall.a: You take part in a realistic conversation — choosing appropriate responses as it unfolds — and then summarise what was discussed.

recall.q: What should you do if you miss one word in dictation?
recall.a: Type the rest correctly and make your best guess for the gap — a near-complete, correctly-spelled sentence still scores.

recall.q: What mainly determines your score on the listening tasks?
recall.a: Accurate spelling and sustained attention — Listen and Type is effectively a precise transcription task.
